jackie-waltman.text: Candidate statement: as a council member she will focus on "maintaining safe neighborhoods, supporting our police, fire, and emergency services, practicing responsible fiscal stewardship, improving infrastructure, protecting local businesses." Cites 30 years in law enforcement.

source.title: Jackie Waltman candidate statement, Burbank City Council 2026 (City Clerk statement, mirrored by BurbankVotes.com)

jackie-waltman.text: Names affordable housing and rent stabilization her lead priority: a housing strategy that "protects renters, supports responsible housing providers, and helps build more affordable homes," noting she has been both a renter and a landlord. Previously served on Burbank's Tenant-Landlord Commission.

source.title: Platform & Key Issues - Jackie Waltman (campaign site)

jackie-waltman.text: Platform: prioritize "responsible development" and preserving each neighborhood's character; "Growth should strengthen communities, not come at their expense."

source.title: Platform & Key Issues - Jackie Waltman (campaign site)

source.title: Platform & Key Issues - Jackie Waltman (campaign site)

samantha-wick.text: Housing: "Utilize smart targeted growth to meet our state housing mandate of homes 8772 by 2029, not blanket density that disrupts neighborhoods"; complete neighborhood-specific plans; expand homeownership, "not just rentals."

source.title: Samantha Wick for Burbank City Council 2026 (campaign site)

samantha-wick.text: Supports "tenant protections under AB 1482 while expanding housing voucher programs" and "continuing the conversation our current council has started. Housing is a human right."

source.title: Samantha Wick for Burbank City Council 2026 (campaign site)

samantha-wick.text: Supports "a mixed-flow approach" to the Olive Avenue Bus Rapid Transit project "rather than a permanent single dedicated lane," to maintain parking and visibility for local businesses.

source.title: Samantha Wick for Burbank City Council 2026 (campaign site)

samantha-wick.text: Per HeySoCal's forum report, Wick, a Burbank planning commissioner, backed mixed-flow traffic for the Olive Avenue BRT, citing Public Works concerns about waste collection.

samantha-wick.text: "Our police and fire departments should always be fully staffed and fully equipped... Public safety is not negotiable - no exceptions." Also wants expanded mental health and crisis response partnerships.

source.title: Samantha Wick for Burbank City Council 2026 (campaign site)

samantha-wick.text: Wants to "strengthen partnerships with our studio partners to create jobs and keep our entertainment industry union members working" and support local businesses.

eddy-polon.text: Housing plan: small-lot ownership and mixed-use housing on city-owned land; promote "missing middle" duplexes and triplexes; require a portion of new housing near transit to be affordable to middle-income (80-120% AMI) households; update codes, including single-staircase reform.

source.title: Eddy Polon's Vision for Burbank (campaign issues page)

eddy-polon.text: Calls for "stronger tenant protections to prevent displacement and stabilize rents for long-time residents."

source.title: Eddy Polon's Vision for Burbank (campaign issues page)

source.title: Eddy Polon's Vision for Burbank (campaign issues page)

eddy-polon.text: Per HeySoCal's forum report, Polon proposed part-time dedicated bus lanes on Olive Avenue using parking lanes during rush hour, noting three of the four cities on the route found a compromise.

eddy-polon.text: Climate: expand tree canopy; incentivize solar, water conservation and drought-tolerant landscaping; invest in electric buses, EV charging and clean fleet transitions.

eddy-polon.text: Supports "full staffing and modern equipment for first responders" and a city government "welcoming of community oversight."
